newsitem.title: INDIA: Israel's Weizman tells Indian Jews to migrate.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Weizman tells Indian Jews to migrate.

text.p: Visiting Israeli President Ezer Weizman on Friday invited the small Jewish community in India to migrate to their fatherland.
"Come to Israel," he told a gathering of Jews in Bombay. "I believe that the immigrants can live the life of a Jew... much better in Israel than in India."
He said life was tough in Israel but the 25,000 Israelis of Indian origin had contributed much to the economy.
"It's an open invitation. We're very happy," said Ezra Moses, secretary-general of the Council of Indian Jewry, a representative body of the community. There are about 5,500 Jews in India.
Moses said it was not better opportunities but the "pull" of the fatherland that lured Indian Jews to Israel.
Weizman said Israel had taken in nearly 700,000 Jews from Eastern Europe in the past seven years -- more than the total population of 600,000 when the country was created in 1948.
Today it had 4.7 million people, Weizman said.
Leading a team of 20 industrialists and businessmen, Weizman was in Bombay, India's financial capital, on the final leg of his India tour. He returns home on Saturday.
